This Criminal Appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 14-A of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, challenging the order dated 02.04.2025,
passed in M.C.A. No. 255 of 2025, by the learned Special Judge (SC/ST), Dumka, by which prayer for regular bail made on behalf of the appellant, namely Prem Kumar Yadav has been rejected in connection with Dumka (T) P.S. Case No. 149 of 2023, corresponding to SC/ST P.S. Case No. 17 of 2024, instituted for the offences under Sections 376/420 I.P.C. and 3/4 of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

3. Heard Mrs. Vani Kumari, learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. Prabir Kr. Chatterjee, learned Spl.P.P. and Mr. Durga C. Mishra, learned counsel for the Informant.
4.
It is submitted that the impugned order passed by the learned Court below rejecting the bail of the appellant is illegal and not sustainable in law.
It is submitted that the appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence and has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that the appellant is the husband of the daughter of the Informant and the Informant is the father-in-law of the appellant.
It is submitted that the appellant is still ready to keep his wife and her child with full dignity and honour.
It is submitted that the Informant has admitted that the appellant was married to his daughter in the Kali Mandir as per social and religious customs on 18.09.2022.
It is submitted that the appellant is in custody since 07.07.2025 and hence, the appellant may be enlarged on bail 5.
On the other hand, learned Spl.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail.
6. Learned counsel for the Informant has also opposed the prayer for bail.
It is submitted that the appellant has resiled from his promise and he is Neutral Citation No. ( 2025:JHHC:31374 ) not keeping the daughter of the Informant and their child.

It is submitted that several witnesses,
including the victim girl and Shashikala Devi, Geeta Devi, Santosh Kumar Hari and Dhiran Hari,
whose statements are recorded in Paragraph No.s 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9 of the Case Diary, have supported the allegation against the appellant and hence, the prayer for bail made on behalf of the appellant may be rejected.
7.

Perused the F.I.R. and the Case Diary and considered the submission of both sides.
8.
It appears that the appellant has performed marriage with the daughter of the Informant and she has given birth to a child.

However, cognizance has been taken against the appellant under Sections 376(2)(n)/420 of I.P.C.
and under Sections 3(1)(w)(i)/3(2)(va) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
9.

sentences.text: During the course of argument, learned counsel for the appellant, after taking instruction from her client, has submitted at Bar that the appellant is still ready to keep his wife and the child with full dignity and honour, if he is being released from the jail.
10. It further appears from the statement of the witnesses that the marriage between the daughter of the Informant and appellant has taken place in a Kali Mandir as per social and religious customs.

11.

Case No. 149 of 2023, corresponding to SC/ST P.S. Case No. 17 of 2024, to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-I-cum-Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Dumka/or his Successor Court, subject to the condition that the appellant shall keep his wife and the child with full honour and dignity.
